Incident Bot: 🚨 PAGER: SEV=high — gpu-pool-3 (us-west-2) exhausted. Autoscaler metrics delayed; queue growth observed for inference-queues (>3x baseline). Start triage. thread_ts=1729999999
Sam (oncall): I'm on it. pulling metrics and rollout history now.
Priya (SRE): grabbing prometheus + metrics-adapter logs. seeing `adapter scrape latency` spikes. possible backlog causing HPA to miss metrics.
Jorge (Platform Eng): Any customer-facing timeouts yet?
Maya (Customer Success): A few customers reported slow responses around 08:12 PT, one reported 504s. I marked a handful as "investigating" in status page.
Sam (oncall): summary from prometheus: `kube_custom_metrics_adapter_errors_total` ramped at 08:10, scrape queue length > 300. HPA for inference-deployments shows `Unknown` for current metrics.
Priya (SRE): logs from metrics-adapter: `E0824 08:10:12.345 adapter.go:142] scrape timeout; upstream backlog` and repeated `429` from prometheus proxy. Likely backlog in ingest or exporter throttling.
Jorge (Platform Eng): checking nodepool autoscaler events — GKE autoscaler reports scale-ups attempted but throttled by quota and maxNodes setting. nodepool `gpu-pool-3` has maxNodes=12, currentNodes=12. queue backlog + no metrics => HPA didn't request additional pods.
Sam (oncall): immediate mitigations: 1) temporarily increase nodepool maxNodes (if allowed) 2) manual scale of critical deployments to relieve queue 3) restart metrics-adapter to unstick scrapes 4) throttle noncritical workloads. I'm going to attempt (3) and (2) now.
Jorge (Platform Eng): I can bump maxNodes by 4, need 2 approvals for quota increase — but quick manual resize is possible if cluster autoscaler accepts. Initiating resize to +4 nodes.
Sam (oncall): executing manual pod scale for the busiest inference deployment:
```
kubectl -n inference scale deployment inference-fast-worker --replicas=10
kubectl -n inference scale deployment inference-batch-worker --replicas=6
```
Sam (oncall): Restarting metrics-adapter to clear scrape backlog:
```
kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart deployment metrics-adapter
kubectl -n kube-system get pods -l k8s-app=metrics-adapter -w
```
Deploy Bot: :rocket: Canary fallback activated for tiered-model-routing: model-variant=small-1 routed for 20% of requests to reduce GPU pressure.
Priya (SRE): After restart, metrics-adapter logs show `scrape worker reinitialized` at +45s and scrape latency dropping. Prometheus now reachable but some series still delayed.
Sam (oncall): Observed HPA for inference-fast-worker transitioned from `Unknown` -> `Active` and started scaling decisions. queue length slowly decreasing.
Maya (Customer Success): Notifying impacted customers: posted update to status page with ETA and mitigation steps. key customers A,B,C notified via email.
Jorge (Platform Eng): Manual nodepool resize accepted by cloud provider — +4 nodes provisioning; should be ready in ~4-8 min. I also set nodepool maxNodes to 20 as temporary safety.
Priya (SRE): Found root cause hypothesis: prometheus forwarder experienced a GC+backlog under high-cardinality custom metrics (per-model counters), and metrics-adapter timed out while waiting for responses. We're working on a follow-up to reduce cardinality and increase scrape parallelism.
Sam (oncall): Quick customer impact estimate: roughly 8 customers experienced >5s median latency increases, 2 customers saw intermittent 504s for ~12 minutes. No data loss reported.
Maya (Customer Success): Keeping the public status update: "Degraded — We are mitigating GPU autoscaling delays causing increased inference latency. Workaround and nodes being added; customers may see improved latency shortly."
Deploy Bot: automated rollback of noncritical GPU workloads executed to free capacity.
Priya (SRE): Action items I'm taking now: 1) follow up on prometheus scrape config + reduce cardinality 2) add longer scrape timeouts and adapter retry logic 3) create auto-remediation to restart adapter if scrape backlog exceeds threshold.
Sam (oncall): Handoff to Priya in 20 min. Current state: manual scales applied, nodepool +4 in progress, metrics-adapter restarted and recovering, HPA resumed. Queue length down ~65% from peak.
Priya (SRE): ACK — I'll own escalation and postmortem. Sam, please leave any logs/commands you ran in the incident doc.
Sam (oncall): copied commands & notable logs to incident doc: `incidents/1729999999` (internal).
Maya (Customer Success): I'll send a targeted message to the 2 customers who saw 504s, with remediation steps and timeline.
Jorge (Platform Eng): follow-up notes: create guardrail to prevent nodepool maxNodes being set too low for expected baseline; consider alert when autoscaler fails due to `maxNodes` cap.
Priya (SRE): status update 08:35 PT — degraded -> partial-recovery. Autoscaler decisions normalizing.
Sam (oncall): marking on-call handoff at 08:40 PT to Priya. leaving a short runbook: 
- What happened: metrics-adapter scrape backlog + nodepool max cap -> HPA missed metrics -> scale didn't trigger -> queue growth -> GPU exhaustion.
- Immediate mitigations performed: metrics-adapter restart, manual pod scaling, nodepool resize +4, disabled noncritical GPU workloads, canary fallback to smaller model.
- Next steps for Priya: postmortem, prometheus config changes, automated adapter restart, evaluation of model routing thresholds.
Priya (SRE): taking over. I'll follow up with a timeline and assign owners. Thanks Sam.
Maya (Customer Success): I'll close the customer notifications once Priya confirms full recovery.
Deploy Bot: :white_check_mark: automated cleanup job scaled noncritical workloads back down after capacity normalized.
Priya (SRE): final update 08:48 PT — metrics pipeline stable, HPA fully functional, queue near baseline. Moving incident to "resolved (monitoring)". Will open postmortem ticket and link in this thread.
Maya (Customer Success): updating status page to: "Resolved — latency returned to normal, no further action required at this time." Customers A/B/C confirmed improved performance.
Sam (oncall): Thanks team. Handing off Slack watch to Priya.
Priya (SRE): Confirmed. Closing thread watch but keeping incident ticket open for postmortem and follow-ups.
